heading: Incomplete representation alignment results from shared training rather than shared structure in the world
definition: alignment stays far from complete and may plateau, and shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain it.
summary: Independent studies find incomplete alignment, sometimes leveling off, and establish that alignment depends on training objectives and task overlap. Whether shared training explains convergence rather than shared world structure remains unresolved; removing physical information from the data also affects alignment.

suggested_status.by_scale: ? for the full causal claim at <1B, 1-10B and 10-100B; ? above 100B because no explicit size bucket records tests there. Toy results are conditional and include perfect-alignment counterexamples; counts have no separate toy bucket.
suggested_status.reason: The full conjunction remains unresolved. Objective/view and task-overlap interventions establish training dependence, while physics-subspace removal establishes a physical-content contribution; these do not discriminate the exclusive causal account. Counts: versions.V7.studies_tested, versions.V7.verdicts, versions.V7.studies_by_size and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation show broad tests of components, not a test establishing that shared training explains convergence rather than shared world structure. Relevant anchors are arXiv:2610.39302#R1–R4, arXiv:2505.13899#R23/#R30 and arXiv:2509.19453#r27–r30.
suggested_status.open_questions: A discriminating causal design separating shared examples, objectives, architecture, initialization and world-generating structure; matched replication of plateau findings under fixed metrics and inputs; longer parameter-scale sweeps; explicit >100B and preference/RL-stage coverage.

source.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis
source.authors: Minyoung Huh; Brian Cheung; Tongzhou Wang; Phillip Isola

original_result.setup: The original study measured image–caption alignment on WIT using the overlap of nearest neighbors (mutual-nearest-neighbor alignment).
original_result.result: Cross-modal alignment reached only 0.16 against a theoretical maximum of 1. CLIP showed higher alignment with explicit language supervision, and ImageNet classification fine-tuning reduced it.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: An exclusive causal decomposition showing that shared data or objectives explain convergence while ruling out contributions from shared world structure, architecture, initialization and optimization.
untested.basis: Objective/view interventions establish training dependence, while physics-subspace removal establishes a physical-content contribution; neither supplies the exclusive decomposition. The health-model header leaves shared training population versus physiology unresolved, and its row is used only for coverage. Anchors: arXiv:2610.39302#R1–R4, arXiv:2505.13899#R23/#R30, arXiv:2509.19453#r27–r30, arXiv:2605.07407#R2. Counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation records interventions but does not identify such a factorial causal test.

untested.what: An asymptotic ceiling for overall alignment as practical foundation-model parameter scale or capability increases.
untested.basis: The width sweep, finite generator budget, recent-model extrapolation and absolute-neuron-count trajectories do not establish an overall asymptote. Anchors: arXiv:2307.12941#R1, arXiv:2609.34732#R2/#R3, arXiv:2604.18572#R12–R17, arXiv:2606.03990#r1/#r3. Counts: versions.V7.coverage_by_operation.scaling describes finite tested coverage, including explicit size buckets only through 10-100B.

untested.what: Explicitly size-stratified V7 tests above 100B parameters.
untested.basis: Counts: versions.V7.studies_by_size and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation contain no >100B category. The displacement study explicitly leaves the largest frontier systems outside its analysis. Unspecified sizes prevent interpreting this as proof that every model was below that threshold.

untested.what: Explicitly stage-stratified effects of preference optimization or reinforcement learning on completeness, plateaus and their causes.
untested.basis: Counts: versions.V7.studies_by_stage and versions.V7.coverage_by_operation contain no preference/RL category. Base, instruct/chat, fine-tuned and reasoning coverage does not identify a controlled preference/RL-stage comparison.

wording_issues.issue: Completeness needs an observable and reference. Near-native face-verification performance after linear mapping does not establish representation completeness; some information does not transfer. Unpaired sentence retrieval, embedding CKA and selected valence directions measure different aspects of agreement. The bge-large / UAE-Large-V1 / mxbai-embed-large-v1 cluster has almost-perfect CKA of 0.98–0.99, challenging substantial incompleteness in that condition. Selected valence directions have cosine 0.939 and mean cosine 0.961 under the reported Procrustes transformation, opposing incompleteness within those selected comparisons. These findings do not establish completeness of whole representation spaces under other measures.

Alignment changes with depth and training stage. LM CKA is 0.875 before decision versus 0.274 afterward, and 0.944 at a middle layer versus 0.000 at the embedding layer; the strong pre-decision and middle-layer values qualify 'far from complete'. MRI cross-family final-layer CKA decreases from 0.61–0.72 pretrained to 0.19–0.46 after fine-tuning; within-family values are separate comparisons. Instruction-tuning effects differ between Gemma and Qwen: Gemma-2-2b-it has mean corrected agreement 0.670 and base–instruct agreement 0.882, whereas Qwen base–instruct agreement is 0.983.

The axis must be specified: training time, test-input quantity and width have distinct finite-range plateaus or fitted ceilings. Fitted below-one test-input ceilings support V7's plateau component; richer inputs do not establish a limitation of that component. ResNet20 seed pairs show incomplete, approximately constant neuron-basis alignment over tested widths, without establishing an asymptotic ceiling for overall representations. Absolute matched-neuron counts show no saturation over their tested parameter ranges, but those counts do not measure an overall alignment asymptote. The permissive wording does not require a plateau on every axis.

The explanation needs condition-specific qualification. IPCL AlexNet-GN models share dimensions across different visual diets, but retain shared architecture and objective; zero shared examples is not established. Disjoint geometric task sets retain alignment while shared-world data and autoregressive training remain, so that comparison does not exclude shared training causes. Dataset overlap has little incremental effect after shared pretraining in the tested fine-tuning settings, including LoRA-finetuned Llama-3.2. Object universality has no significant objective or dataset contrasts in the tested SSL ResNet-50, SLIP, ImageNet and CLIP groups. Conversely, Taskonomy ResNet-50 objectives significantly modulate universality with architecture and data held fixed, supporting an objective contribution there.

wording_issues.phrase: rather than a common model of reality
wording_issues.issue: The exclusion exceeds the tested contrast. Physics-subspace removal reduces alignment relative to random removal. Objective and overlap interventions demonstrate training effects without establishing that shared world structure contributes nothing. The cited task-overlap experiments with ViT/tiny and ResNet152 fine-tune pretrained weights; they do not train those models from scratch.

The evidence supports conditional contributors, including architecture, optimization or implicit bias, and modality-specific information. Alternative-optimizer results demonstrate optimizer dependence; imperfect inner-product alignment does not establish absence of shared subspaces or linear mappability. Idealized EDLNs at entropic-objective global minima have perfect alignment, a restricted theoretical counterexample to incompleteness. Within either MRNS or MWNS, the same function and input data yield identical RSMs, also challenging incompleteness; static across-function correlations do not establish completeness. Correlational family or corpus comparisons do not identify an exclusive cause.

method_sensitivity.factor: Local versus global geometry and distance-agreement criteria
method_sensitivity.what: LM neighborhood-weighted RSA changes with neighborhood scale. Requiring strict distance agreement leaves much less WIT alignment than relational overlap alone. For DINOv2-base against the validation LLM panel, cross-modal ceiling-relative bands are 51–58% for RSA and 83–92% for CKA; these are population bands, not OpenLlama-3b pair values. Coarse CKA gives partial evidence for V7 incompleteness, while the contrast demonstrates V6 metric dependence. Low-level VLM global dependence, local overlap and held-out coordinate mapping give different assessments; substantial but incomplete alignment is observed evidence for V7.

Video alignment changes with frame count and caption diversity. VATEX fitted saturation parameters are S∞ ≈ 0.41 with R² = 0.9791 for VideoMAEv2 Huge, and S∞ = 0.365 with R² = 0.9964 for DINOv2 Giant. These are fitted extrapolations supporting input dependence and below-one saturation. Richer inputs do not establish a limitation of V7 or test its training-data/objective explanation. DINOv2–OpenLlama mutual-kNN decreases with larger/different galleries. Mamba-1.4B–Pythia-1.4B unwhitened CKA is 0.52 on FineWeb-Edu versus 0.78 on LAMA TREx. Lexical RSA is stronger for frequent words but remains incomplete, supporting V7 incompleteness and V6 input dependence.

method_sensitivity.factor: Objective construction, class count and training stage
method_sensitivity.what: ResNet-50 CL–NSCL CKA is 0.87 versus CL–SCL 0.043, and changes with class count and temperature. MRI cross-objective-family linear CKA declines from pretrained AD 0.61–0.72 and MCI 0.63–0.71 to fine-tuned AD 0.19–0.45 and MCI 0.34–0.46. These exclude within-family pairs. Coupling labels to selected patch-energy components changes first-layer profile similarity; component 3 gives correlation 0.76, supporting component-dependent training effects. During RNN learning, full-pretraining models become more similar to Master while models with no pretraining-task overlap become less similar. Partial-overlap ranks show no graded differences; this still supports coarse training-history dependence under V7.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training corpus, positive views and teacher targets
method_sensitivity.what: DINOv3 student alignment rises toward its fixed teacher while falling toward independent models. Scientific encoders can group more by training dataset than architecture. Captioner-written versus text-only-paraphrased JEPA training text changes WIT alignment from 0.107 to 0.060. REEF distribution-merging comparisons give Fusellm-7b versus source Openllama-2-7b CKA 0.6713 and versus source Mpt-7b 0.6200; Fusechat-7b versus source Internlm2-chat-20b 0.9278, Mixtral-8x7b-instruct 0.9701 and Qwen-1.5-chat-72b 0.9991. Shared-target causation is inferred, without isolation from initialization, lineage or other training differences; fused-output training details are not supplied.

method_sensitivity.factor: Layer, architecture width and instruction tuning
method_sensitivity.what: ANN–SNN CKA is below 0.2 for a large portion of ResNet-164 layers, supporting V7 incompleteness; most wide ResNet-20 ×8 layers on CIFAR-10 exceed 0.8, without an established near-completeness threshold. LM CKA is 0.875 before decision versus 0.274 afterward: observed stage dependence, with partial V7 support at the pre-decision stage. Truth-category base–instruct agreement differs between Gemma and Qwen. Gemma-2-2b-it mean corrected agreement is 0.670, while its agreement with its base is 0.882; pairwise significance does not test that mean. Visual instruction tuning qualitatively reduces LLaVA vision-side alignment with LLMs relative to original CLIP encoders. This supports tuning sensitivity, without establishing a V2 capability trend.

method_sensitivity.factor: SAE extraction, matching, budget and denominators
method_sensitivity.what: Joint rotation-conditioned extraction increases measured BERT universality more than post-hoc rotation of independent SAEs; percentages concern features active in both models. In fixed-backbone SAEs with 32,768 latents, sharing requires the same counterpart in encoder and decoder matchings, with cosine ≥0.7 in both. About 35% remain orphan relative to all eight other seeds, averaged over base SAEs, supporting V7 incompleteness. Cell F at full budget gives operator explained fractions 0.57 whole and 0.47 masked. The budget sweep measures nearest-neighbour decoder overlap: 0.198 for cell F at 199,999,488 activations and 0.307 for a narrower configuration at 100,941,824 activations. Overlap increases with budget; operator-transport budget sensitivity is untested. Cross-architecture validation rates concern pre-selected matched pairs.

Qwen3 bridge cosine decreases from rank-8 to full-rank projection. Gemma2-2B–27B global token-geometry correlation is 0.39 while intrinsic-dimension correlation is −0.09, demonstrating observed metric dependence and incomplete alignment under V6 and V7. Raw Alpha changes under function-preserving ReLU rescaling. Substrate alignment changes with retained rank and probe-domain composition. The within-discriminative versus within-MAE/MIM alignment ratio narrows to 1.22× under changed probe composition: observed V6 dependence, but partial V7 support because objective-group separation persists.

method_sensitivity.factor: Mapping, evaluation split and compatibility selection
method_sensitivity.what: Recommendation Linear Map training-item R² is 0.171 versus Identity −0.076, while unseen-item transfer fails. Adapter results are conditioned on screening for native linear compatibility; screened-out ridge comparisons show observed incomplete native linear alignment under V7, alongside absent usable correspondence under V4. Llama–Mistral Procrustes cosine is 0.530 with 140 anchors; the globally reported unaligned reference is −0.002, without a separate holdout baseline. CCA gives complete retrieval despite incomplete Procrustes cosine; complete retrieval does not establish complete whole-representation alignment. Supervised orthogonal Procrustes vision-to-language concept retrieval improves log-linearly with language-model size over the tested range, without observed saturation; later plateaus and shared-training causes are untested.

method_sensitivity.factor: Initialization, optimizer, noise and solution type
method_sensitivity.what: Random-initialization LM similarity exceeds trained-model similarity in the reported controls. Idealized EDLN entropic-selection global minima establish perfect alignment, a restricted theoretical challenge to V7; weight decay and generic gradient flow show observed optimizer dependence without deciding general linear mappability. Analytical similarity depends on solution type: for the same function and input data within MRNS or MWNS, identical RSMs challenge V7 incompleteness. Static across-function correlations do not establish completeness. CCE theory gives below-one correlation at finite SNR and sample ratio, with alignment vanishing at interpolation. Empirical alignment has a sharp minimum near γ≈1 and is lower at smaller SNR in both sample-size regimes, supporting the tested V7 incompleteness component.

method_sensitivity.factor: Null calibration, neighborhood scale and scaling statistic
method_sensitivity.what: FEMBA–DINOv2 raw mKNN rises with FEMBA size, but a circular-shift null preserving temporal structure tracks that trend. Excess neighborhood alignment over that control is described as modest. The calibrated size trend is absent under V1; calibration dependence is observed under V6, and temporal smoothness contributes to apparent convergence under V7. This does not establish a causal explanation of all alignment. Calibrated image–text neighborhood capability correlations are 0.82–0.87 at k=10,20,50; mKNN rises at k=10 but plateaus for larger models at k=100. These correlations do not measure completeness or training causes. Mutual-top-1 Rosetta-neuron counts grow sublinearly through language models up to 30B and vision models up to 5B while matched fractions shrink; overall alignment asymptotes are untested.
